## What FESV does

`FESV` performs covariate selection in two-way fixed effects panel models:

$$
y_{it} = \alpha_i + \gamma_t + \mathbf{x}_{it}^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}
        + \varepsilon_{it}.
$$

The unit effects $\alpha_i$ and time effects $\gamma_t$ are **held fixed**:
they are partialled out and are never candidates for selection. The candidate
covariates are the *players* of a cooperative game whose characteristic
function is

$$
v(S) = \text{Adj-R}^2(S \mid FE) - \text{Adj-R}^2(\emptyset \mid FE),
\qquad v(\emptyset) = 0.
$$

Because the adjusted $R^2$ penalises degrees of freedom, adding an irrelevant
covariate *lowers* $v$, so noise players receive negative Shapley values. The
Shapley value of covariate $j$ is its average marginal contribution over all
coalitions:

$$
\phi_j = \sum_{S \subseteq N \setminus \{j\}}
  \frac{|S|! (p - |S| - 1)!}{p!}
  \left[ v(S \cup \{j\}) - v(S) \right].
$$

## Worked example on simulated data

```{r}
library(FESV)
set.seed(1)

N <- 40; T <- 15
unit <- rep(1:N, times = T)
time <- rep(1:T, each = N)
beta <- c(0.8, 0, 0.6, 0, -0.5, 0)
X <- matrix(rnorm(N * T * length(beta)), ncol = length(beta))
colnames(X) <- paste0("x", 1:length(beta))
y <- as.vector(X %*% beta) + rnorm(N * T) + unit * 0.5 + time * 0.3

res <- fe_shapley_covariate_selection(y, X, unit, time,
                                      exact = TRUE, gamma = 0.01)
```

### Shapley values

```{r}
sort(res$shapley_values, decreasing = TRUE)
```

The active covariates `x1`, `x3`, `x5` have clearly positive values, while the
noise covariates `x2`, `x4`, `x6` have values at or below zero.

### Selection rules

```{r}
res$selected_sign    # Rule A: phi_j > 0
res$selected_nested  # Rule B: nested penalised criterion
```

Both rules recover the true active set.

### Efficiency identity

The sum of the Shapley values equals the grand coalition value $v(N)$:

```{r}
res$efficiency_gap
```

### Diagnostics

```{r}
res$superadditivity
res$core
```

## Bootstrap inference

```{r, eval = FALSE}
boot <- bootstrap_shapley(y, X, unit, time, B = 999)
boot$ci
boot$se
```

## Real-data application

The package ships three country panels. Run the full workflow on the pooled
sample:

```{r}
data(all_panel)
d <- all_panel
X  <- as.matrix(d[, c("FDI", "INF", "POP", "TOP", "UR", "EXR")])
out <- fe_shapley_covariate_selection(d$Income, X, d$id, d$year,
                                      exact = TRUE, gamma = 0.01,
                                      verbose = FALSE)
sort(out$shapley_values, decreasing = TRUE)
out$selected_nested
```

## References

Shapley, L. S. (1953). A value for *n*-person games. In H. W. Kuhn and
A. W. Tucker (Eds.), *Contributions to the Theory of Games*, Vol. 2, Princeton
University Press, 307-317.

Ko, H. (2026). *Shapley-Value Covariate Selection for Panel Data Models: A
Cooperative Game-Theoretic Approach.* Working paper.
